question: Does the observed AC1018 TABLE value flag 0x16 have a documented meaning, and can libdxfrw preserve it without treating unknown bits as complete semantics?

authority.source: Open Design Specification for .dwg files v5.4.1
authority.fields: TABLE flag-for-value is BS/group 90; ODA identifies 0x06 as the normal has-block flags, 0x10 as table direction, and 0x20 as title-suppressed.

physicalPeer.result: The parser reports a complete 3x3 plain-text grid and retains all seven 10-bit cell override ranges plus the 4-bit TABLE override range. The source has an unrelated HEADER integrity warning.

implementation.behavior: The legacy TABLE parser marks flags outside the ODA-described 0x06/0x10/0x20 profile incomplete while retaining the bounded frame. The AC1018 direct encoder accepts zero or the documented base flags with direction/title bits and emits the selected value unchanged. The existing generated body vector exercises 0x16; unsupported 0x40 is rejected for output.
controls: Generated AC1018 value flag 0x16 parses completely and survives direct body write/readback exactly.
Generated AC1018 unknown value flag 0x40 remains typed but semantically incomplete; the same parser then reads a corrected frame.
The same-object writer refusal for 0x40 preserves seeded body/handle buffers and accepts corrected 0x16.
implementation.physicalProbe: build-gcc/libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip --inspect-physical-table-codec /private/tmp/libdxfrw-table-ac1018-oda/out/acad_table_simple.dwg confirms source flag 0x16 and the exact eight retained ranges. Direct source-body encoding remains refused, including when the range metadata or value flag is independently removed from a copy; other source-model admission conditions remain unresolved.

validation.result: The build and focused selector pass. Direct-source inspection confirms the exact peer profile and continued refusal; it is diagnostic research, not a passing source-output qualification.

disposition: Closes only recognition and bounded preservation of documented legacy value-flag bits. It does not qualify direct physical-source TABLE output, native semantics/rendering, or broader TABLE producer profiles. The peer DWG remains scratch-only; no drawing fixture was added.
